description: rt analyze complexity command: cyclomatic, cognitive, LOC, and parameter-count metrics per method with rollup to type/namespace and configurable threshold.

userStories.title: Add rt analyze complexity command
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run rt analyze complexity --solution X to get cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, LOC, and parameter count per method across the solution, so that I can identify hotspots for refactoring.
acceptanceCriteria: ComplexityCommand class exists at src/RoslynTools/Commands/ComplexityCommand.cs as internal sealed class ComplexityCommand : IRtCommand
ComplexityCommand.Info.Name equals "complexity" and matches the first argument passed to new Command(...) in Build()
ComplexityCommand.Info.Category equals "analyze"
ComplexityCommand.Info.JsonOutput is true
ComplexityCommand.Info.Mutates is false
ComplexityCommand.Info.Examples contains at least one runnable invocation including rt analyze complexity --solution RoslynTools.slnx
Running rt analyze complexity --help prints help text describing --solution, --threshold, --sort, and --top flags
rt analyze complexity is reachable both as rt analyze complexity and as the unqualified rt complexity form, matching the existing convention enforced by App.RunAsync
dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx succeeds with zero errors after ComplexityCommand is added
dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes exits 0 after ComplexityCommand is added
dotnet test RoslynTools.slnx -v minimal passes with the new ComplexityCommand tests included
The startup registry assertion in App.cs does not throw when ComplexityCommand is reflection-discovered (Info.Category is one of the accepted values)
With a valid --solution path, command exits 0 and writes a single JSON document to stdout
With a valid --solution path, all progress and diagnostic messages are written to stderr, never stdout
Stdout JSON parses successfully via System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse with no trailing or leading non-JSON text
JSON root object contains a methods array, a typeRollups array, and a namespaceRollups array

Each entry in methods contains exactly the keys method, type, namespace, file, line, cyclomatic, cognitive, loc, params with correct JSON types (string/string/string/string/number/number/number/number/number)
method field is the fully qualified method name including the containing type (e.g. RoslynTools.Core.WorkspaceLoader.OpenAsync)
type field is the fully qualified containing type name without the method portion
namespace field is the containing namespace string, or an empty string for types in the global namespace
file field is an absolute path to the source file containing the method declaration
line field is the 1-based line number of the method declaration opening in file
For an empty method void M() {}, cyclomatic equals 1 (base path)
For a method with a single if statement and no else, cyclomatic is 2 (base + 1 decision)
For a method with if / else if / else, each if and else if increments cyclomatic by 1; bare else does not add to cyclomatic
For a method with a switch containing N non-default case labels, cyclomatic increases by N over the base
for, foreach, while, and do-while loops each contribute +1 to cyclomatic
Each catch clause contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ternary (?:) operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ?? null-coalescing operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ?. null-conditional member access contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each && and each || binary logical operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ??= null-coalescing assignment operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Non-default pattern switch expression arms each contribute +1 to cyclomatic; the default discard arm _ does not
cognitive for an empty method is 0
cognitive adds +1 per structural break (if, switch, loop, catch, ternary) at the outermost nesting level of the method body
cognitive applies a nesting multiplier: a structural break at nesting depth d adds 1 + d (e.g. an if directly inside a method body at depth 0 adds 1; the same if nested inside another if adds 2)
cognitive adds +1 for each else or else-if clause that interrupts linear flow
cognitive adds +1 for each transition between binary logical operator types in a sequence (e.g. a && b || c counts as 2: one && sequence and one || sequence), not +1 per individual operator
cognitive adds +1 for each direct recursive call to the enclosing method
loc counts only non-blank, non-comment physical lines inside the method body braces
loc for void M() {} is 0
loc for a method containing only return; on one line is 1
loc excludes lines consisting solely of // single-line comments
loc excludes lines that fall entirely inside a /* ... */ block comment and contain no executable tokens
loc excludes the opening and closing brace lines of the method body when those lines contain no tokens other than the brace
loc for an expression-bodied method int M() => 1; is 1
params equals the number of formal parameters declared on the method signature
params for static int M(this string s, int x) (an extension method) is 1, not counting the this parameter
params for a parameterless method is 0
Constructors are included in the methods array with method set to TypeFQN.ctor (or equivalent clear convention) and metrics computed as for regular methods
Property accessors get, set, and init are each included as separate entries with method names using a TypeFQN.PropertyName.get / .set / .init convention
Local functions declared inside a method body are reported as separate entries with method names scoped to their enclosing method
Lambda expressions and anonymous methods are NOT reported as separate entries; their complexity is folded into the enclosing named method or accessor
Abstract method declarations and partial method declarations without bodies produce no entry in methods
Auto-implemented properties with no explicit accessor body produce no entry in methods
Source files containing an <auto-generated> header comment are skipped entirely
Source files with a .g.cs or .Designer.cs suffix are skipped entirely
typeRollups entries contain type, namespace, methodCount, cyclomaticTotal, cognitiveTotal, locTotal, paramsTotal fields
typeRollups totals equal the sum of the corresponding per-method metric values for all methods of that type (across all methods, not just filtered ones)
namespaceRollups entries contain namespace, methodCount, cyclomaticTotal, cognitiveTotal, locTotal, paramsTotal fields
namespaceRollups totals equal the sum of the typeRollups values for all types in that namespace
With --threshold 0 (default), every analyzed method appears in the methods array
With --threshold 5, a method where every metric value is strictly less than 5 is excluded from the methods array
With --threshold 5, a method where cyclomatic equals exactly 5 is included (>= comparison, not >)
With --threshold 5, a method where cognitive is 7 but all other metrics are below 5 is included
--threshold does not affect typeRollups or namespaceRollups totals; rollups are always computed over all analyzed methods regardless of the threshold filter
--threshold -1 exits with code 1 and a descriptive stderr message stating the threshold must be >= 0; no JSON is written to stdout
--sort cyclomatic (the default) orders the methods array by cyclomatic descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort cognitive orders the methods array by cognitive descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort loc orders the methods array by loc descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort params orders the methods array by params descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort with an unrecognized value exits with code 1 and a stderr message listing the accepted values (cyclomatic, cognitive, loc, params); no JSON is written to stdout
--top 0 (default) does not truncate the methods array
--top 5 truncates the methods array to at most 5 entries after sorting is applied
--top N where N exceeds the total method count returns all methods without padding or error
--top -1 exits with code 1 and a descriptive stderr message; no JSON is written to stdout
--top truncation does not affect typeRollups or namespaceRollups; rollups still cover all methods
With no --solution flag and exactly one .sln or .slnx file in the current working directory, the command auto-detects it and proceeds successfully
With no --solution flag and no .sln or .slnx file in the current working directory, the command exits with code 1 and a stderr message indicating that no solution file was found
With no --solution flag and multiple .sln or .slnx files in the current working directory, the command exits with code 1 and a stderr message listing the candidate paths
--solution pointing to a path that does not exist exits with code 1 and a stderr error message; no unhandled exception propagates
--solution pointing to a file that exists but is not a valid solution exits with code 1 and a stderr error message; no unhandled exception propagates

Running rt analyze complexity --solution RoslynTools.slnx completes successfully, exits 0, and the JSON output includes at least one entry in methods referencing a method from the RoslynTools source (dogfood)
A solution that compiles but contains zero method declarations produces a JSON document with empty methods, typeRollups, and namespaceRollups arrays and exits 0
Async methods (async Task) are analyzed and the await expression does not add to cyclomatic or cognitive beyond the surrounding control structures
Iterator methods using yield return are analyzed and yield return / yield break do not add to cyclomatic or cognitive beyond surrounding control structures
--sort and --threshold and --top flags may all be combined in a single invocation and each behaves independently: threshold filters first, sorting is applied to filtered results, then top truncates
Tests are located under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/ in an Analyze subfolder (or the matching existing analyze test folder convention) and use with_<scenario>_<outcome> naming
Tests use a real .slnx fixture and do not mock the Roslyn workspace, compilation, or syntax tree APIs

Test suite includes cases for: empty method cyclomatic baseline, each decision branch type (if, switch case, for, foreach, while, do-while, catch, ternary, ??, ?., &&, ||, ??=, pattern switch arm), extension method param exclusion, threshold filtering (below, equal, above), each sort option, top truncation, auto-detect success / fail / ambiguous, missing solution path
After implementation, rt dump-help output lists analyze complexity with --threshold, --sort, --top, and --solution flags plus at least one example
rt analyze complexity --solution RoslynTools.slnx --top 10 exits 0 in under 60 seconds when run against the roslyn-tools solution
userStories.notes: New ComplexityCommand.cs in src/RoslynTools/Commands/. IRtCommand contract: Category=analyze, JsonOutput=true, Mutates=false. Metrics: cyclomatic (decision branches), cognitive (nesting-weighted), LOC (non-blank non-comment lines in body), params (excl. this for extensions). Flags: --threshold 0 (show all, >= filter), --sort cyclomatic|cognitive|loc|params, --top N. JSON output: methods[] + typeRollups[] + namespaceRollups[]. Rollups always cover all methods regardless of threshold/top. Solution auto-detection via existing pattern.
